correctness.rationale: Every two-spin marginal entry is affine in \(z=e^{2h}\) after fixing all other interactions, and \(\operatorname{Cov}=4\det(M)/(\sum M)^2\); consequently at most two sign changes for all finite \(N\). For three spins, exact hyperbolic-cosine factorization yields \(Az^2+Bz+C\) with signs of \(A,C\) determined by \(a\pm d\). The positive-root cases and the identically-zero polynomial follow algebraically. A logarithmic interaction example has roots \((193\pm15\sqrt{161})/32\) and both conditional pair odds ratios equal 2, proving sharpness. A packaged standard-library checker passed 4188 independent finite assertions; finite tests do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-interaction dependence-nucleus framework naturally raises the question of how observable pair association can change under external-field shifts. The dimension-free maximum number of changes is sharp, all three-spin crossing regimes have necessary-and-sufficient algebraic criteria, and the explicit two-reversal witness demonstrates positive conditional association can turn negative then recover. This is a complete structural classification rather than an arbitrary single numerical invariant.
